title: How the enemy reads a soldier: a 1942 Army training film
desc: Combat Counterintelligence is a 1942 U.S. War Department training film. This episode follows the whole arc of its argument: how an enemy gathers information from photographs, tracks, letters, careless talk and the things a soldier carries, and the discipline the film asks for. Several scenes are acted, and the narration says so. The narration voice is synthetic; the archival film is unaltered. Source: U.S. War Department, Signal Corps, Official Training Film 11-321, public domain.
